Lithium Price Analysis: Carbonate Holds 142,750 Yuan After Recent Pullback
data.description:
Battery material has seen a modest correction in the past session, adding 1,250yuan or 0.88%, as the overall trend leans toward consolidation after a robust first-half rally. Battery-grade lithium carbonate prices have been volatile as supply and demand fundamentals change across the market.

Lithium Price Finds Support After Lengthy Pullback

The 1-year chart of lithium carbonate illustrates a healthy rebound from late 2025 levels before a correction ensues. Prices increased rapidly in the first few months of 2026 before reaching the levels of almost 200,000 yuan/tonne in May and then easing back to the present 142,750 level.

The diagram shows that LIT is finding a higher band than its 2025 lows. Following the May peak, prices retraced through June and July to create a downward trend. The recent advance towards 142,750yuan reflects the market testing a support zone after falling away from the previous rally.

Today’s daily movement: 0.88% higher as lithium carbonate rebounds from the recent sideways trading sessions. Price has been trading inside a narrow price band near recent lows, indicating lower price volatility relative to the drastic range trading seen earlier in the year.

The short-term structure has resistance building in the 150,000-160,000 yuan area. Above this zone, it would be a greater correction, whereas if it remains weak, it would be targeted towards a lower support area.

Lithium Carbonate Technical Indicators Show Neutral Momentum

Meanwhile, the TradingView chart for other lithium-related assets appears to have a neutral technical setup. The MACD indicator moved to the middle after previous buying momentum weakened. The latest values read MACD 0.01 and histogram -0.08.

This is a sign that the momentum is slowing down after the recent push. The directional indicator is not showing a strong directional movement.

However, the RSI is at about 49.75. The RSI is still at the moderate 50 levels and remains somewhat away from its earlier heavy values, signaling that lithium is no longer witnessing the kind of momentum it had witnessed in the previous rally.

The graph of the lithium stock index displayed another significant intraday move to 242.43. The stock fluctuated primarily between 235 and 238 during the session. The move was enough to take the index away from the recent lows, although momentum indicators showed signs of easing.

Lithium Market Tracks Supply And Demand Shifts

Nonetheless, the lithium carbonate market is still closely following revisions to battery demand, inventory levels, and activity in production. According to market information, lithium prices have recovered from earlier lows and are back up to levels below those seen at the 2026 high earlier this year.

Price evaluations conducted over the past three months highlight the continuing vulnerability of battery-grade lithium carbonate to supply responses to demand from the electric vehicle and energy storage markets.

What is important here, because of the current chart structure, is 142,750 yuan as short-term support. Maintaining this level preserves the recent consolidation scheme; breaking below could carry us down even further.

On the positive side, lithium carbonate has to return to the 150000 yuan level in order to restore a bullish stance in the short term. Overall, the market is still in the consolidation area between the recovery moves and the correction after the May peak.

data.title: Canadian Tire Corporation Supports Canadian Wildfire Relief Efforts Through $200,000 Donation to the Canadian Red Cross
data.description:
Customers across Canada will also be able to support relief efforts at participating banners

TORONTO, Aug. 8, 2026 /CNW/ -- As wildfires continue to impact communities across Canada, Canadian Tire Corporation (CTC) is supporting relief efforts through a $200,000 donation to the Canadian Red Cross' Canadian Wildfire Fund, and enabling customers to support through in-store donations across its network of banners.

The fundraising campaign will help the Red Cross provide national emergency assistance to people and communities affected by wildfires, including support for urgent needs and recovery efforts as the season continues. As a long-standing partner of the Canadian Red Cross, CTC has seen first-hand the important role that community support can play during moments of crisis.

Starting Saturday, August 8, customers across Canada will be able to contribute to wildfire relief efforts by donating at checkout at participating Canadian Tire, Mark's, SportChek, Pro Hockey Life and PartSource locations. Donations at participating Gas+ locations will begin Tuesday, August 11. All customer donations will go directly to the Canadian Red Cross.

"When communities are facing a crisis, timely support is critically important," said Jonathan Anderson, AVP, Community Impact, Canadian Tire Corporation. "In addition to CTC's corporate donation, the support of our Dealers, employees and customers across the country will help advance the crucial work of the Canadian Red Cross and ensure people and communities can access urgent assistance as quickly as possible."

"Across Canada, communities are facing significant challenges as wildfires continue to impact their lives," said Melanie Soler, Vice President, Emergency Management, Canadian Red Cross. "We are grateful to Canadian Tire Corporation for their generous support and for providing this opportunity for their employees and customers to help people impacted by wildfires. These donations to the Canadian Red Cross will help communities prepare for, respond to, and recover from wildfires in Canada."

Canadians can support current emergency relief efforts online through the Canadian Red Cross website or in-store at participating CTC banner locations nationwide.

ABOUT CANADIAN TIRE CORPORATION

Canadian Tire Corporation, Limited, (.A) () (or "CTC"), is a group of companies that includes a Retail segment, a Financial Services division and CT REIT. Our retail business is led by Canadian Tire, which was founded in 1922 and provides Canadians with products for life in Canada across its Living, Playing, Fixing, Automotive and Seasonal & Gardening divisions. Party City, PartSource and Gas+ are key parts of the Canadian Tire network. The Retail segment also includes Mark's, a leading source for casual and industrial wear; and sports retailers SportChek, Sports Experts, Pro Hockey Life, Hockey Experts, and Atmosphere, which offer the best-in-class brands in active wear and sports gear. The Company's over 1,600 retail and gasoline outlets are supported and strengthened by CTC's Financial Services division and the tens of thousands of people employed across Canada and around the world by CTC and its local dealers, franchisees and petroleum retailers. For more information, visit Corp.CanadianTire.ca.

MEDIA INQUIRIES

mediainquiries@cantire.com, 416-480-8453

SOURCE Canadian Tire Corporation, Limited

Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures

This press release includes certain non-GAAP financial measures. The reconciliations of such measures to the most comparable GAAP figures in accordance with Regulation G are included herein.

Berkshire presents its results in the way it believes will be most meaningful and useful, as well as most transparent, to the investing public and others who use Berkshire’s financial information. That presentation includes the use of certain non-GAAP financial measures. In addition to the GAAP presentations of net earnings, Berkshire shows operating earnings defined as net earnings exclusive of investment gains (losses), impairments of goodwill and intangible assets and other-than-temporary impairments of equity method investments.

Although the investment of insurance and reinsurance premiums to generate investment income and investment gains or losses is an integral part of Berkshire’s operations, the generation of investment gains or losses is independent of the insurance underwriting process. Moreover, as previously described, under applicable GAAP accounting requirements, we are required to include the changes in unrealized gains (losses) of our equity security investments as a component of investment gains (losses) in our periodic earnings statements. In sum, investment gains (losses) for any particular period are not indicative of quarterly business performance.

Berkshire Hathaway and its subsidiaries engage in diverse business activities including insurance and reinsurance, utilities and energy, freight rail transportation, manufacturing, services and retailing. Common stock of the company is listed on the New York Stock Exchange, trading symbols BRK.A and BRK.B.
